solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Usually in a hot, steamy novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so the letters before it are made into something new

explanation.surface: A bookish homebody curled up with a racy romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being read, but it signals the anagram of A HOT STEAMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone usually in is a homebody, a person who seldom goes out.

clue.text: School welcomes university of a similar kind

indicators.note: a school that welcomes someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A school opens its doors to a like-minded university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomes' puts U inside SCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in 'such people' means people of that sort, of a similar kind.

clue.text: Ring as reminder of a flapper caught in shady walk

parts.note: ALAR means relating to wings, and a wing is a flapper

indicators.note: caught sits in the shady walk, so its letter goes inside that word

parts.note: a mall is a sheltered, tree-lined walk, like the Mall in London
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A 1920s flapper girl is collared on a tree-lined promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapper' suggests a 1920s girl, but here it is a wing; the rare adjective for wings supplies the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A wake-up ring from a clock or phone is a reminder sounded at a set time.

clue.text: Leader brought down in pontifical outrage

indicators.note: the first letter, the leader, is moved lower down the word, as this is a down clue

parts.note: papal means relating to the Pope, the pontiff

explanation.surface: A church leader is toppled amid papal fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader brought down' takes the first P of PAPAL and moves it one place down, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrage someone is to shock and horrify them, a synonym.

clue.text: My struggle to lift up poles

parts.note: to heave is to haul something up with great effort
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A weightlifter grunts while straining to raise a pair of poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation of surprise, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, as in 'My, what a sight!'

clue.text: Manipulator has misgivings about surface-to-air missile in revolution

indicators.note: a thing in revolution turns round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: someone who rues something regrets it
SAM is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A political fixer has doubts about a rocket during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is just a link (regretting regarding the missile); 'in revolution' turns the whole RUESSAM backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur works the body with the hands, literally a manipulator of muscles.

clue.text: Take over stadium, say

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a bowler takes an over, delivering six balls
an amphitheatre-shaped arena, like the Hollywood one

explanation.surface: A tycoon plans to seize control of a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one player, so to take an over is to deliver it.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is the cricket action of delivering; the noun is an arena, like the Rose arena at Pasadena.

clue.text: Dislike top conductor's stand

indicators.note: to top something is to cut off its top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a conductor stands on a podium

explanation.surface: An orchestra's star maestro is unpopular on his platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like an adjective for the conductor, but it is a verb removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread hatred or disfavour, a strong synonym.

clue.text: One not fully involved in order of course including soup

definitions.text: One not fully involved in order

indicators.note: the course word includes the soup, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a course of bricks is a layer
broth is a thin soup

explanation.surface: A diner half-attends to the menu when soup arrives among the courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a meal, but here it is a row of bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastic order's lay members do manual work without taking full holy orders.

clue.text: Crush top sportsman

definitions.meaning: to munch or mash noisily, as a horse does at the bit
short for a title holder, the winner

explanation.surface: A victor flattens the opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means chew or mash; the noun is short for champion, the leading sportsman.

clue.text: An American domain removing right or (separately) banning luxury

parts.note: an gives A
US for the United States

indicators.note: the domain word has these letters taken out of it

parts.note: a domain is a territory

explanation.surface: A US state outlaws extravagance, while dropping a right or two.
explanation.walkthrough: '(separately)' tells you R and OR come out of TERRITORY at different points: TER(R)IT(OR)Y leaves TERITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerity is a regime of strict economy in which indulgences are given up.

clue.text: E. coli shot, tested initially in a piece of cake

indicators.note: the initials sit in the piece of cake, inside it

parts.note: a piece of cake means easy

indicators.note: initially means take the first letters of the words named

explanation.surface: A lab finds bacteria in a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E.' looks like the start of the bacterium's name but is the definition: E is slang for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: E is street slang for the party drug MDMA, also known by this name.

clue.text: Dramatist accepting dishonesty, to a greater extent

indicators.note: one word accepts the other, taking it inside

parts.note: more means to a greater degree
a lie is a piece of dishonesty

explanation.surface: A playwright welcomes ever more deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière was the great seventeenth-century French comic playwright.

clue.text: Person bringing a case to carry millions for region now in Iraq

indicators.note: the litigant carries the millions inside

parts.note: a suer brings a lawsuit
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A litigant hauls a fortune off to the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a suitcase of money, but it is a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient civilisation of southern Mesopotamia lay in what is today Iraq.

clue.text: Females in crush for Rocket Man

indicators.note: the females go in the crush phrase, inside it

parts.note: step on means crush underfoot
hens are female birds

explanation.surface: Women in a mob of fans for the Elton John song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket Man' suggests the Elton John hit, but it is George Stephenson, whose locomotive was the Rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stephenson built the Rocket, the pioneering 1829 steam locomotive.

clue.text: Crackpot rages at irritant

indicators.note: crackpot means crazy, so the letters following are jumbled

explanation.surface: An eccentric shouts angrily at something annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackpot' seems to be the person raging, but it signals the anagram of RAGES AT.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas is used in riot control because it stings the eyes, an irritant by design.

clue.text: Norwegian heroine embraces male who takes risks

indicators.note: the heroine embraces the male, holding him inside

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the heroine of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: An Ibsen heroine hugs a reckless man.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bets or chances things on uncertain outcomes is a risk-taker by nature.

clue.text: Make more changes to a part behind study

indicators.note: the other pieces come behind, after the study word

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: An actor revises a role after learning it.
explanation.definitionFit: To readapt is to alter again, adjusting once more to new conditions.

clue.text: Raving at young, an adviser dealing with problems

indicators.note: raving means wild or mad, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone ranting at the youth, a counsellor tackling their troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raving' signals the anagram of AT YOUNG AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine columnist who answers readers' letters about personal troubles.

clue.text: Sound equipment on boom, perhaps for controversial argument

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it

parts.note: a boom is an example of a pole
MIC is short for microphone

explanation.surface: A sound crew sets a microphone on a boom.
explanation.walkthrough: A boom is the long pole holding a microphone over a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a fierce written or spoken attack, a combative argument.

clue.text: Sole (fixed) income earner?

parts.note: reads like a household's only steady breadwinner, but this tradesman earns money from mended shoe bottoms

explanation.surface: The family's only wage earner on a fixed income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like 'only', but means the underside of a shoe; this shoe repairer earns by fixing them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe mender makes a living repairing soles and heels.

clue.text: Endless publicity over plugging only a small opening for viewer

indicators.note: the reversed piece plugs the gap, going inside the other word

parts.note: sole means only

indicators.note: over signals that the trimmed word is turned round
endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: hype is publicity

explanation.surface: Constant promotion plugging just one tiny peephole for a spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves HYP; 'over' turns it round; 'plugging' sets the result inside the word for only. 'plugging' also hints at publicity, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A peephole in a door lets you look through it, a small opening for watching.

clue.text: Ship carries funny Dickensian transported to Australia

indicators.note: the ship carries the funny word inside it

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
queer means strange or funny

explanation.surface: A convict ship bears an odd Dickens character to Botany Bay.
explanation.walkthrough: In Nicholas Nickleby the cruel schoolmaster Wackford Squeers is sentenced to transportation, the old penalty of exile to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Wackford Squeers, the Dotheboys Hall head in Nicholas Nickleby, ends up sentenced to transportation.

clue.text: Message rejected among Israeli-Americans

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters run backwards
the word sits among the letters of the words given

explanation.surface: A note is turned down by a group of Israeli-Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' finds LIAME inside IsraeLI-AMEricans; 'rejected' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a message sent over a network.

clue.text: A mountain hectare

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
HA is the abbreviation for hectare

explanation.surface: A mountain measured at a hectare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like the article but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek alphabet stands for A, and it is the NATO code word for that letter.

clue.text: Such thinking isn't clouded by practicalities

definitions.text: Such thinking isn't clouded by practicalities

parts.words: Such thinking isn't clouded by practicalities
parts.note: creative, unconstrained ideas are named after a cloudless heaven

explanation.surface: A remark about visionary, impractical brainstorming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clouded' plays on the cloudless image the phrase evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of thinking is imaginative and unhampered by real-world limits, like a cloudless heaven.

clue.text: Muscle is shown up, recently developed

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: new means recently made

explanation.surface: A newly built muscle on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is the tissue joining muscle to bone; the word also means muscular strength.

clue.text: Sound from some Persians?

indicators.note: a sound from means the letters are said aloud and heard as a like-sounding word
some of the word, its opening letters only

explanation.surface: A question about a noise made by people from Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three letters of Persians, said aloud, match the noise; and Persian cats make that noise, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A contented cat makes a low continuous vibrating noise, and Persians are a breed of cat.

clue.text: EU rules changed with limits for pig sticker

indicators.note: changed means the letters are altered into a new order
limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Brussels regulations revised on the tools for killing hogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits for' gives PG, the outer letters of pig, which join EU RULES in the anagram that 'changed' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong adhesive is something that sticks things, a sticker.

clue.text: One aquarium regularly overlooked Pacific location

indicators.note: letters at regular intervals are skipped, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A single fish tank keeps being missed in an ocean-front spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly overlooked' drops O, E, Q, A, I, M, leaving the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny island republic lies in the Pacific Ocean, in Micronesia.

clue.text: Life preserver on ancient ship

parts.note: sounds like a lifebelt aboard an old vessel, but means the biblical patriarch who saved all creatures on the Ark

explanation.surface: A lifebuoy hanging on an old galleon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life preserver' suggests a lifebelt; it is the man who preserved animal life in the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch built the Ark and saved his family and pairs of every animal from the Flood.

clue.text: Saltiness isn't evident in this wordplay for Ewart

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay: a fresh arrangement of the letters of the name Ewart

explanation.surface: A note on a puzzle about a man called Ewart, with no salt in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as cryptic wordplay: 'fresh' is an anagram signal, and its fodder spells Ewart.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers and lakes hold water without salt, the opposite of seawater.
